summary: Two gaps a consumer hit while composing the bar across five app surfaces. (1) THE 48px HEIGHT WAS EMERGENT, NOT PINNED. The bar was py-sm around whatever its tallest child happened to be, which silently assumed a 32px control was present — so a bar whose tallest child is a 24px Header.Item rendered at 40px, and one route in an app had a shorter app bar than every other with nothing to say so. Both public call sites had already worked around it with their own h-12. The component now owns the height its own sheet specifies (h-12); py-sm stays, as the 32px content lane the sheet draws its controls in. The browser test mounts a bar containing nothing 32px tall and asserts 48. (2) Header.Item COULD NOT CARRY target/rel. Its props extended HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, which has no target, no rel, no download and no referrerPolicy, so an item pointing off the app could not open in a new tab through its own API — the only route was the `render` slot, which means writing the href twice and keeping the two copies in step. They now extend AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>. `type` is the one anchor attribute removed: on the button branch it is the type="button" that stops a nav item submitting a form around it, and on an anchor it is a MIME hint nothing here wants.

migration.manual: A bar with no 32px control in it grows from its emergent height to 48px. If your app added its own `h-12` to compensate, remove it — the class merges either way, so leaving it is harmless. An external Header.Item routed through `render` purely to reach target/rel can drop the render element and pass target/rel directly.
